skill.name: python-env
skill.description: Manage Python projects with uv, including environments, dependencies, lockfiles, tools, packaging, and publishing workflows.
skill.summary: Use uv to create, sync, run, package, and publish Python projects with reproducible environments.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples for uv commands, package metadata URLs, cache paths, and publishing workflows. Two real concerns remain: the skill metadata recommends a curl-to-shell uv installer, and the publishing reference documents PyPI token storage in ~/.pypirc.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh in the compatibility metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell command with safer installation options, such as package manager commands or downloading the installer for review before execution.

remediation.issue: Publishing documentation shows PyPI tokens in ~/.pypirc.
remediation.suggestion: Lead with trusted publishing and clearly warn users not to commit or expose .pypirc files. Use scoped tokens and placeholders only.

remediation.issue: The skill can guide agents to run uv commands that modify dependencies and lockfiles.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to review dependency changes and lockfile diffs before committing updates made through the skill.

static_findings.snippet: # Build sdist + wheel — uv has a native builder, no separate `build` install
# Dev tooling → dependency-groups (PEP 735). `uv add --dev <pkg>` writes here;
# `uv sync` installs it by default. Not shipped with the published package.
# Opt-in extras users install explicitly: `uv add "my-package[docs]"`
(`uv add` / `uv sync` / `uv run`) over the `uv pip` compatibility layer — it
manages `pyproject.toml` + a lockfile for you and is reproducible.
| Start a project | `uv init <name>` (app) · `uv init --package <name>` (installable, `src/` layout)
| Add dev dependency | `uv add --dev pytest ruff` |
| Run in project env | `uv run pytest` |
| Install a CLI tool | `uv tool install ruff` · one-shot: `uvx ruff` |
`uv init` creates `pyproject.toml`, pins a Python version, and prepares the
project for `uv add` / `uv sync`. The `--package` (src) layout is preferred for
`uv` creates and manages `.venv` automatically — you rarely activate it; just
uv run -- ruff check .      # `--` ends uv flag parsing
Never call bare `python` / `pytest` / `ruff` in a uv project — they may resolve
to a different interpreter. Always `uv run`.
Use `uv tool` / `uvx` for developer CLIs (ruff, pre-commit, httpie). Use
`uv add` only for things your code imports.
is a sensible floor for new projects (TaskGroup, `Self`, faster interpreter).
# Dev deps live here; `uv add --dev <pkg>` manages this group.
`uv pip` mirrors pip's interface for environments uv doesn't manage (a hand-made
venv, a legacy `requirements.txt`, CI that isn't uv-native). It does **not**
update `pyproject.toml` or the lockfile — prefer `uv add` / `uv sync` whenever
| Pin project Python | `uv init --python 3.12` or edit `requires-python` |
| Lock/resolve conflict | `uv lock --resolution=lowest-direct` to probe, then loosen bounds |
- `uv add` / `uv remove` / `uv sync` for project dependencies (not `uv pip install`)
- `uv run` to execute anything inside the project env
- `uv tool install` / `uvx` for standalone developer CLIs
- `uv pip` only for environments uv doesn't manage

content.value_statement: Python projects often drift across virtual environments, lockfiles, and package tools. This skill gives Claude and Codex clear uv workflows for setup, dependency changes, execution, packaging, and publishing.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use uv project workflows instead of uv pip compatibility commands.
Provides commands for creating projects, adding dependencies, syncing environments, and running tools.
Shows pyproject.toml patterns for libraries, CLIs, FastAPI apps, tooling, and build systems.
Documents dependency workflows for lockfiles, requirements files, workspaces, private indexes, and Git dependencies.
Guides package build, TestPyPI validation, PyPI publishing, versioning, and CI publishing patterns.
limitations: Requires the uv CLI to be installed before commands can run.
Does not verify package trust, license compliance, or dependency vulnerability status.
May modify pyproject.toml, uv.lock, or environment state when commands are executed.
Publishing guidance still requires the user to configure PyPI projects and credentials safely.

use_cases.title: Create a reproducible Python project
use_cases.description: Set up a uv-managed project with pyproject.toml, uv.lock, dev tools, and a pinned Python version.

use_cases.title: Modernize dependency management
use_cases.description: Move from ad hoc pip commands or requirements files to uv add, uv sync, and lockfile-based workflows.
use_cases.target_user: Maintainer of an existing Python repository

use_cases.title: Prepare a package release
use_cases.description: Build distributions, validate artifacts, test installation on TestPyPI, and publish with modern PyPI practices.

prompt_templates.title: Start a new uv project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-env skill to create a new uv-managed Python project for a small command line app. Explain each step before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Add dependencies safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-env skill to add runtime and development dependencies with uv. Show which files should change and how I should review them.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a legacy environment
prompt_templates.scenario: Migration from pip or requirements files
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-env skill to inspect this Python project and recommend a uv workflow. Include how to handle requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, and lockfiles.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a package for publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-env skill to prepare this package for a PyPI release. Check build metadata, versioning, TestPyPI validation, and safer publishing options.

output_examples.input: Set up a new Python package with uv and pytest.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes a uv package layout, initializes the project, adds pytest as a dev dependency, and explains the resulting pyproject.toml and lockfile changes.

output_examples.input: Why should I use uv run instead of pytest directly?
output_examples.output: The assistant explains that uv run uses the project environment, while a bare command can resolve to a different interpreter or global tool.

output_examples.input: Help me publish this package safely.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks build metadata, recommends TestPyPI validation, explains trusted publishing, and warns against exposing local token configuration.

best_practices: Use uv add, uv remove, uv sync, and uv run for projects that uv manages.
Review pyproject.toml and uv.lock changes before committing dependency updates.
Use trusted publishing for PyPI releases when your hosting platform supports it.
anti_patterns: Do not mix bare pip commands with uv-managed project dependencies.
Do not run global python, pytest, or ruff when the project expects uv run.
Do not store or commit real PyPI tokens in project files or shared examples.

faq.question: Does this skill install uv automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides uv workflow guidance and commands. Users should install uv through a trusted method before using the commands.

faq.question: Can it replace pip completely?
faq.answer: It recommends uv project workflows for most active projects. It still documents uv pip for legacy or unmanaged environments.

faq.question: Will it update my lockfile?
faq.answer: Yes, commands such as uv add, uv remove, uv sync, and uv lock can update uv.lock or environment state.

faq.question: Does it support monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include uv workspace patterns for multiple packages in one repository.

faq.question: Can it help with publishing to PyPI?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers build artifacts, TestPyPI checks, versioning, changelogs, CI, and trusted publishing concepts.

faq.question: Does it audit dependencies for vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It manages environment workflows, but it does not perform dependency vulnerability or license audits.
